title: VEX art pipeline
question: How does a PNG drawn by an artist become pixels on the pedal without touching C++?
summary: Artists edit PNG strips, a manifest (with optional play sequences) and a theme in art/. tools/make_sprites.py validates them, prints what each animation step costs the panel and generates sprites.h, anim.h, theme.h and two font headers. ui.h renders on a 100 ms cadence; flush.h finds the changed rows, the Teensy sends only those bands and reports flush_us and tx_bytes over serial.

steps.title: Draw in art/
steps.body: PNG strips of 32 x 32 frames, manifest.json timing and play sequences, theme.json colours.

steps.title: Import and validate
steps.body: tools/make_sprites.py rejects off-palette pixels, partial alpha, wrong strip sizes, frame periods that are not multiples of DISPLAY_MS and out-of-range sequences, writes the committed headers and prints the step cost.

steps.title: Render and flush
steps.body: ui.h quantises time to DISPLAY_MS; flush.h compares rows with the shadow buffer; the .ino writes only the dirty bands over SPI, times the flush and can stream the bands to the workbench Device tab.
